transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Ivy Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Hale (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (CTO - Arbor Analytics), Evan Park (ML Engineer), Priya Natarajan (Head of Security)

Summary: brief discovery to map model selection needs; conversation touches on long-context summarization, live tool-calling for CRM updates, multilingual requirements, and security/regulatory needs.

00:00 Ivy Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate you taking the time today. quick intros?
00:08 Sofia Ruiz: sure i'm sofia, cto at arbor, we build an analytics platform for urban planning, we have a lot of long reports and mixed language inputs, english/spanish mainly, some chinese.
00:18 Evan Park: evan, ml infra, i'll be running tests and integrate once we pick a path.
00:23 Priya Natarajan: priya, security lead, i'll focus on data residency and key mgmt.
00:28 Ivy Chen: awesome. and on our side Marcus is the se who will dig into perf and tool-calling examples.
00:35 Marcus Hale: hi all, excited to dig in. given the use case — long reports + multilingual + some tool/actioning — there are a few model tradeoffs to discuss. do you have a target latency or cost per request?
00:48 Sofia Ruiz: for interactive features we want sub-1s token latency ideally for short queries, but for full-document summarization we can tolerate a few seconds. cost-wise we want predictable unit costs; we're worried about token bloat with 32k contexts.
01:05 Evan Park: also we plan to do retrieval-augmented generation that calls our vector DB and occasionally writes back (e.g., update flags). tool-calling important.
01:15 Marcus Hale: okay good. so primary axes: context length (8k vs 32k), multilingual accuracy, and tool-calling. host vs dedicated vs private depends on SLOs and data controls. quick Q: how many concurrent users and what percent of requests are long-context?
01:28 Sofia Ruiz: peak concurrent is ~120 API clients during business hours; ~15% of requests are full-report summaries that use long contexts, the rest are short queries.
01:40 Marcus Hale: that helps. for 120 concurrent with 15% long requests, Dedicated pool with reserved capacity could give predictable throughput. Hosted works if you can accept burst limits and less isolation. Private/VPC if you need keys never to leave your network.
01:55 Priya Natarajan: on private, are there options for HSM/KMS integration? we require customer-managed keys for PII processing.
02:03 Ivy Chen: yes, our Private offering supports KMS/HSM integrations and we can provide audit logs. Dedicated also supports KMS with an enterprise contract; hosted supports BYOK for token encryption at rest in certain tiers. we'll share the KMS integration guide.
02:17 Evan Park: question about models: do you host open models only, or do you have custom fine-tuned variants? multilingual capability is a must — spanish quality needs to be near parity with english.
02:28 Marcus Hale: Redwood provides a model catalog of curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. we also offer model variants and can onboard custom fine-tuned weights in Dedicated/Private. for multilingual needs, we typically recommend testing a 32k multilingual model if the long docs include multiple languages, since you avoid chunking artifacts.
02:45 Sofia Ruiz: chunking is painful for us — we lose discourse coherence. but cost is a concern; 32k models look more expensive per token. can you quantify?
02:55 Marcus Hale: rough example — for a 10k token document, a 32k model avoids chunking and extra prompt tokens. cost difference comes from model speed and token billing; we can run a perf run on our infra using your sample docs to estimate token/time cost. i'll put together 32k vs 8k run comparisons.
03:12 Ivy Chen: also consider intelligent KV/prefix caching and batching — Redwood Optimize can reduce unit cost for repetitive prefixes. for summary pipelines caching earlier chunks sometimes helps.
03:24 Evan Park: how mature is tool-calling? we need function calls that can do retrieval, call our crm, and write small updates. reliability very important.
03:33 Marcus Hale: function/tool-calling is supported; we can show examples where the SE wires the model to tool stubs (retrieval, DB write). the runtime supports structured outputs and we recommend using schema-based function outputs to reduce hallucinations. we'll demo a flow next week.
03:50 Priya Natarajan: security-wise we need SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and data residency options for EU customers. also SOC 2 Type II and iso27001 are required.
04:03 Ivy Chen: we have SOC 2 and ISO reports; SSO/SAML and RBAC are standard on enterprise plans, audit logs available in Redwood Console. we can provide SOC 2 report under NDA.
04:12 Sofia Ruiz: what about private deployment? we have some on-prem customers and regulatory constraints. could Redwood run in our VPC or on-prem?
04:20 Marcus Hale: yes — Redwood Private can deploy a control plane with customer-managed networking, and we offer an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. note that on-prem can increase ops overhead and lead times. dedicated gives a middle ground — reserved GPU pool in a vendor-managed environment but with network isolation options.
04:38 Evan Park: another nit — quantized model support and performance. we want to run faster cheaper without big loss in quality, esp for retrieval tasks.
04:46 Marcus Hale: our serving runtime supports quantization-friendly paths and will select kernels accordingly. we can run quality regressions vs your eval set to pick the right quantization profile. Redwood Optimize has model and quantization recommendations per workload.
04:58 Sofia Ruiz: multilingual eval — can you run Spanish/Chinese prompts? we have evaluation sets and human labels.
05:04 Marcus Hale: yes send a small eval set (10-20 documents in each language) and we'll include it in perf runs. that will give objective metrics and human-eval samples.
05:14 Priya Natarajan: data retention? logs and transcripts — we need configurable retention and ability to scrub PII.
05:22 Ivy Chen: configurable retention windows, and data can be excluded from retention for Private deployments. we also support log redaction and provide APIs for deletion requests.
05:32 Sofia Ruiz: any gotchas around latency for 32k models?
05:36 Marcus Hale: larger context impacts memory and throughput; token latency tends to be higher but depends on sequence distribution and hardware. kernel selection and batching help; for interactive short queries you'd want a smaller lower-latency model or route short queries to a low-latency variant. Redwood supports smart routing by request profile.
05:52 Evan Park: smart routing sounds useful. how hard is it to set rules?
05:56 Marcus Hale: it's a config layer — you can route by policy (latency, cost, region, customer tier). we'll share an example routing config.
06:05 Ivy Chen: recap: Marcus will run perf tests (32k vs 8k) on their sample docs + multilingual eval; I'll send pricing for hosted/dedicated/private and SOC2/ISO docs; Marcus will demo tool-calling in a follow-up.
06:18 Sofia Ruiz: yeah that works. timeline — we'd like results in a week to decide whether to pilot.
06:22 Marcus Hale: we can aim for 7 business days.
06:25 Priya Natarajan: i'll also share their internal policy doc for KMS and data residency.
06:29 Ivy Chen: perfect. any final questions?
06:32 Sofia Ruiz: one last: do you allow model pinning and can we freeze a model at a commit for reproducibility?
06:38 Marcus Hale: yes, model versioning and pinning are supported — you can pin a model version and rollout policies. that's standard for Dedicated/Private and available on Hosted through versioned model endpoints.
06:48 Sofia Ruiz: great. thanks all.
06:51 Ivy Chen: thanks everyone we'll follow up with the artifacts. meeting end.

Notes: informal transcription with occasional mis-hearings. references to product names (Redwood Optimize, KV cache, Private) may appear in different capitalizations in transcript.
